Frozen position anchor bank from a set of states

Source: R/anchor_bank.R
position_anchor_bank.Rd

Builds the anchor bank used by position-selected OMRF subsampling from states of a previous (typically full-gradient) chain, for example the online grid snapshots of [read_online_summaries()]. It applies the same rule the sampler uses for its own warmup: coordinate scales are the standard deviations of the states (floored at a tenth of their median), the first anchor is the last state, and further anchors are added by greedy farthest-point selection in the scaled metric.

Usage

position_anchor_bank(
  standata,
  subsampling,
  parameter_names,
  states,
  capacity = 8L,
  metric = c("scaled", "hessian")
)

Arguments

standata

The Stan data of the subsampled fit.

subsampling

The [stan_subsampling()] object of the subsampled fit.

parameter_names

Unconstrained parameter names, in sampler order.

states

Numeric matrix with one state per column.

capacity

Maximum number of anchors.

metric

Anchor selection metric, `"scaled"` or `"hessian"`.

Value

A version-1 position anchor bank specification.

Details

During sampling each state uses the anchor nearest in a shared metric, so the anchor is a function of position and the Voronoi cells are bounded by hyperplanes. `metric = "scaled"` uses the coordinate scales above; `metric = "hessian"` uses the mean likelihood Hessian of the anchors plus the identity, which approximates the posterior precision and so predicts the control-variate error better (it requires global HCV anchors).

Pass the result as `subsampling_position_anchor_bank_spec` to [pdmp_sample_from_stanmodel()], with `subsampling_anchor_selection_policy = "position"`, `t_warmup = 0` and a frozen flow.
